title: Girth Conjecture (strengthening of Theorem 3)
statement_text: For every triangle-free graph $F$, there is a constant $c_F$ and graphs $G$ of arbitrarily large chromatic number and the same girth as $F$ such that every $F$-free induced subgraph of $G$ is $c_F$-colourable.
context_text: Here $G$ is $F$-free if it contains no induced copy of $F$. The authors prove that for every graph $F$ with at least one edge there are a constant $c_F$ and graphs $G$ of arbitrarily large chromatic number with the same clique number as $F$ in which every $F$-free induced subgraph is $c_F$-colourable, generalizing results of Carbonero, Hompe, Moore and Spirkl (disproving the Galvin–Rödl/Esperet conjecture) and of Briański, Davies and Walczak; in particular a triangle-free $F$ yields a triangle-free $G$. It is natural to ask whether $G$ can also have the same girth as $F$; the authors conjecture so but could not prove it, and in their concluding section state the conjecture in the more general form: for every graph $F$ with at least one cycle there are $b_F$ and graphs $G$ of arbitrarily large chromatic number and the same girth as $F$ whose $F$-free induced subgraphs are $b_F$-colourable. As a weaker result, they prove the analogue with odd girth (length of a shortest odd cycle): for every nonbipartite $F$ there are such $G$ with the same odd girth as $F$. A necessary condition, that graphs of girth at least $g$ form a vertex Ramsey class, holds by a theorem of Nešetřil and Rödl. Their construction (adding edges according to residues of distances in a base graph) unavoidably creates many $4$-cycles, so even the case $F=C_5$ would be very interesting.
notes: Stated in prose as 'We conjecture that this is the case, but have been unable to prove it' without a labelled theorem environment. PDF source — math may be garbled. Section 8 is explicitly stated to contain further open problems but is not present in the extracted text.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs of induced subgraphs of large chromatic number
